args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After v2.3.1 was deployed, checkout-api started failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of about 18%. v2.3.1 is marked unhealthy in production, and its release candidate v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging. Action taken: rolled checkout-api back in all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. Post-rollback check: all regions on v2.3.0, healthy, error rate 0.2%. Follow-up: find the root cause in v2.3.1 before redeploying, and look into why it was promoted even though the RC was unhealthy in staging.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's now passing health checks. I also opened a SEV2 incident (INC-0001), which paged on-call.

- **The bad release:** v2.3.1 was failing health checks in us-east, us-west and eu-west, with an error rate of 18%.
- **Version I picked:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. I didn't consider v2.3.1-rc because it only ran in staging, and it was unhealthy there too.
- **After the rollback:** all three regions are on v2.3.0 and the error rate is down to 0.2%.
- **Incident INC-0001:** it covers the failure, the rollback and the check afterwards. As follow-ups, it asks for the root cause in v2.3.1 to be found before anyone redeploys it, and for a look at why v2.3.1 reached production when its release candidate was failing in staging.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0 (v2.3.1 is unhealthy; v2.3.1-rc was staging only).
